projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The persistent presence of 20+ devices combined with zero camera, lighting, or water activity on a Monday morning indicates an unusually still household, likely meaning the family is home but inactive (e.g., sleeping in, illness, or cameras masked). A quick status check is recommended.

The persistent count of 20-21 'mobile' devices alongside zero camera, lighting, or water activity on a Monday morning strongly suggests UniFi is miscounting IoT/smart home devices as mobile, or guests are present but inactive; this sensor artifact may be skewing occupancy-based automations.

A stable presence count of 20-22 devices combined with zero camera, light, or water activity at 8:31 AM on a Monday indicates the household is likely still asleep or away, which is atypical for a weekday morning when daily routines typically begin.

The stable presence count (20-22 devices) combined with zero camera or light activity confirms the household is asleep and the network is simply tracking background devices, with the 03:47 spike aligning with the already-flagged low-severity event.

A new mobile device connected to the network at 03:47 AM and remained active for over an hour without any corresponding camera, audio, or lighting activity, suggesting a device that was previously offline or a quiet presence (possibly a child) rather than active household movement. Worth a quick morning check to rule out forgotten devices or late-night activity.

The presence sensor consistently reports 18–22 mobile devices over the last 34 minutes, significantly exceeding the household's six members. This pattern likely indicates either unannounced guests are over or the network is miscounting smart home/IoT devices as phones, so a quick verification is recommended.

Presence data shows 14-19 connected mobile devices for a four-person household with zero camera activity, suggesting either unannounced guests, a network artifact inflating the count, or everyone remaining stationary indoors; worth a quick verification to rule out connectivity issues or unexpected visitors.

The persistent 1-device fluctuation in mobile presence over two hours, paired with Steve’s severely truncated sleep, indicates he is awake and moving between Wi-Fi zones rather than resting. This ongoing restlessness suggests his sleep disruption is active and may warrant a gentle check-in or environmental adjustment.
Steve slept only 2.44h last night. May be a rough morning — heads up.

The sustained count of 19–21 connected devices alongside zero camera motion for four hours indicates a large group is likely gathered in camera-blind areas or the presence tracker is counting non-human IoT devices. This matters because it confirms the home is occupied despite the cameras, but warrants a quick verification to ensure camera functionality and rule out sensor inflation.
